title: "Sandcastle → Kubernetes hand-off"

## Overview

**Sandcastle → Kubernetes hand-off** is the first runnable lab that
spans the boundary between the **construction** layer and the
**composition** layer of the academy story:

> **Crossplane composes**, **Sandcastle constructs**, **Picos behave**.

You will take the durable Git branch produced by the
[Hello World Pico Sandcastle lab](../hello-world-pico-sandcastle/)
— `sandcastle/hello-world-pico`, containing `rules/hello.yaml` — and
promote its greeting `value` into a Crossplane **Composite Resource**
that the [Hello Pico on Kubernetes lab](../hello-pico-on-kubernetes/)
already knows how to compose onto a real cluster.

This lab is deliberately narrow: it covers only the hand-off itself.
The Sandcastle side is verified by the Sandcastle lab; the cluster side
is verified by the Kubernetes lab. This lab proves the boundary between
them is coherent and automatable.

## What you will produce

A single generated file, `work/handoff-sandcastle-to-kubernetes/build/xr.yaml`,
whose shape is byte-equivalent to the reference
[`05-xr.yaml`](../hello-pico-on-kubernetes/downloads/05-xr.yaml) shipped
with the Kubernetes lab. This is the `produces` entry
`hello-world-pico-on-kubernetes-xr` in
[`metadata.yaml`](metadata.yaml).

The generated XR can be applied unchanged after completing steps 1–4 of
the [Hello Pico on Kubernetes walkthrough](../hello-pico-on-kubernetes/walkthrough.qmd)
(Crossplane, provider, XRD, Composition), which is where cluster-side
verification lives.

## Downloads and screenshots

Runnable files live under [`downloads/`](downloads/):

- [`handoff.sh`](downloads/handoff.sh) — reads the greeting value from
  the Sandcastle-produced branch and writes the Crossplane XR.
- [`expected-xr.yaml`](downloads/expected-xr.yaml) — reference XR shape
  the generated file must match.
- [`verify.sh`](downloads/verify.sh) — automatable check that runs the
  Sandcastle lab (if needed), runs the hand-off, and asserts the
  generated XR matches the Kubernetes lab's `05-xr.yaml` shape.

Screenshots referenced from the walkthrough live under `screenshots/`.
